result.title: SPEM: Structure-Aware Procedural Memory for Efficient Skill Use in LLM Agents
result.summary: LLM-based agents increasingly rely on reusable skills. However, scaling skill libraries makes efficient and accurate skill use difficult. Full skill loading incurs high token and runtime overhead. In contrast, flat semantic retrieval treats skills as independent text entries, ignoring dependencies, execution order, state transitions, and data flow constraints. We propose SPEM, a lightweight structure-aware procedural memory framework for efficient skill use in LLM-based agents. SPEM maintains Atomic Skill Memory for individual skills and Skill-DAG Memory for reusable compositions derived from successful executions. For a new task, SPEM reuses high-confidence Skill-DAG templates when available. Otherwise, it retrieves atomic skills and invokes Skill-GNN for state- and structure-aware skill selection. Successful executions are written back as new Skill-DAGs, allowing procedural memory to accumulate over time. Experiments on ALFWorld and SkillsBench show that SPEM achieves the best overall effectiveness--efficiency trade-off, reaching 87.1% ALFWorld success and 38.38% SkillsBench reward while reducing token and runtime costs against strong baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SPEM，一种面向 LLM agent 的轻量结构化过程记忆：维护原子技能记忆与从成功执行中提炼的可复用 Skill-DAG 组合，优先复用高置信模板，否则用 Skill-GNN 做状态与结构感知的技能选择，并将成功执行回写为新 DAG 以累积记忆。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属 agent 技能库检索领域，与视觉或 latent 推理状态无直接联系；但「依据当前状态与组合结构选择可复用推理片段」的机制，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的复用、候选路径验证与计算分配提供类比线索，可供核查。
